title: Knee joint forces during downhill walking with hiking poles
claims: Eight males walked downhill on a 25-degree ramp with and without hiking poles while kinematic, kinetic and electromyographic data were collected.
With poles, peak and average ground reaction force, knee joint moment, and tibiofemoral compressive and shear forces were significantly reduced by 12-25%.

The reductions came primarily from forces applied to the poles and a more forward-leaning upper body that reduced the knee moment arm; patellofemoral compression, quadriceps tendon force and vastus lateralis activity showed similar but non-significant reductions due to high variability.
This was a downhill walking study in eight males; its load-reduction figures do not transfer directly to trail running.
